big_picture: This line tests oil, European gas and cross-market transmission as part of the wider goal of understanding Henry Hub before prediction or model selection.

historical_facts.does_not_rule_out: A separately designed modern lagged oil signal, European-US transmission test, or regime-conditional cross-market forecast may still contain incremental information.
historical_facts.observed: Roberts/Brown-Yucel source-package evidence reproduced inside rep-012 shows the historical oil-gas linkage is regime-dependent and does not remain stably cointegrated after 2007.
historical_facts.rules_out: Treating a fixed historical WTI-Henry Hub cointegrating coefficient as a stable modern cross-market relation.

programme_interpretation: The core rep-015 literature finding is accounted through shared Roberts source evidence without double-counting an independent experiment. rep-016 remains untested; contextual congestion evidence remains a design constraint.
revisit_trigger: Revisit empirical execution only after applicable HOLD/REDESIGN blockers are resolved, implementation/power contracts are verified, and the operator explicitly authorizes the transition.
selection_basis: Fresh external-literature mapping under programme 002; no legacy internal result is used as scientific calibration or expected outcome.
tested_role_target_horizon: The core oil-gas regime-break finding is internally accounted by the rep-012 Roberts package: rank-one linkage appears in 1997-2007 and disappears in the full/post-2007 samples. This is shared source evidence, not a second independent rep-015 experiment.
why_zoomed_in: Cross-market effects are regime- and infrastructure-dependent and must distinguish contemporaneous linkage from forecastable information.
